title: ✓ UNIT 1: APPLICATIONS OF BIOLOGY
notes: ✓ Biology is applied to conserve natural resources, improve food production, develop medicines, protect the environment, improve agriculture and support industry.

title: ✓ 1.1 CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES
notes:
✓ Natural resources → materials and conditions supplied by nature.

✓ Renewable → can be naturally replaced when properly managed.

◆ Examples → water, forests, crops, animals, sunlight.

✓ Non-renewable → finite resources that are not replaced quickly.

◆ Examples → coal, oil, natural gas, minerals.

✓ Conservation → wise use, protection and management of natural resources.

✓ Conservation biology → protects biodiversity, habitats and endangered species.

title: ✓ 1.2 FOOD & NUTRITION SECURITY
notes:
✓ Food security → reliable access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food for a healthy life.

✓ Nutrition security → adequate food + safe water + sanitation + health care + healthy practices.

✓ Malnutrition includes:
◆ Overnutrition → excessive nutrient/energy intake.
◆ Wasting → low weight for height.
◆ Stunting → low height for age.
◆ Micronutrient deficiency → lack of essential vitamins/minerals.

✓ Biology improves food production, nutrition and food quality.

title: ✓ 1.3 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
notes:
✓ Sustainable development → meeting present needs while protecting resources for future generations.

✓ 3 Main dimensions:
◆ Economic → economic efficiency and viability.
◆ Social → equity, employment and participation.
◆ Environmental → biodiversity and responsible resource use.

✓ Sustainable development = Economic + Social + Environmental well-being.

title: ✓ 1.3.1 BIOLOGY & SUSTAINABILITY
notes:
✓ Biologists contribute by:
◆ Conserving natural resources and biodiversity.
◆ Monitoring soil, water and air pollution.
◆ Developing methods for pollution control.
◆ Improving food production.
◆ Promoting recycling, reuse and waste reduction.
◆ Developing resource-efficient biological technologies.

title: ✓ 1.4 BIOTECHNOLOGY
notes:
✓ Biotechnology → use of living organisms, cells or biological products to produce useful goods and services.

✓ GMO → organism whose genetic material has been modified.

✓ Recombinant DNA → DNA formed by combining genetic material from different sources.

✓ Transgene → gene transferred into another organism.

✓ Transgenic organism → organism containing an introduced gene.

✓ Applications → food • medicine • agriculture • environment • industry.

title: ✓ 1.4.1 FOOD PRODUCTION & FERMENTATION
notes:
✓ Microorganisms are used to produce and preserve foods through fermentation.

✓ Single-cell protein (SCP) → protein-rich microbial biomass used as food or animal feed.

◆ Examples → Spirulina, Fusarium venenatum, Methylophilus methylotrophus.

✓ Fermentation → microorganisms convert organic substrates into useful products.

✓ Applications → yogurt • bread • cheese • fermented meat • beer • wine • traditional Ethiopian foods.

title: ✓ 1.4.2 DAIRY PRODUCTS
notes:
✓ Microbial fermentation produces many dairy products.

◆ Yogurt → Streptococcus thermophilus + Lactobacillus bulgaricus.
◆ Acidophilus milk → Lactobacillus acidophilus.
◆ Cultured buttermilk → lactic acid bacteria.
◆ Sour cream → microbial fermentation.

✓ Fermentation changes acidity, flavor and texture.

title: ✓ 1.4.3 BEER, WINE & SPIRITS
notes:
✓ Beer → malted barley → wort → yeast fermentation → beer.

✓ Wine → fruit juice + yeast → fermentation → wine.

✓ Spirits → fermented material → distillation → concentrated alcoholic product.

✓ Saccharomyces → important yeast used in alcoholic fermentation.

✓ Fermentation → produces mainly ethanol + CO₂.

✓ Distillation → separates alcohol from other components.

title: ✓ 1.4.4 BREAD MAKING
notes:
✓ Saccharomyces cerevisiae → common baker's yeast.

✓ Yeast ferments sugars and produces CO₂, causing dough to rise.

✓ Microorganisms also:
◆ Improve flavor and aroma.
◆ Condition dough.
◆ Help produce the porous texture of bread.

✓ Sourdough → lactic acid bacteria + yeasts contribute characteristic flavor.

title: ✓ 1.5 GENETIC ENGINEERING
notes:
✓ Genetic engineering → deliberate modification or transfer of genetic material.

✓ Transgene → transferred gene.
✓ Transgenic organism → organism containing an introduced gene.

✓ Applications → medicine • agriculture • livestock improvement • research • pest control.

title: ✓ 1.5.1 TISSUE CULTURE
notes:
✓ Tissue culture → growing cells or tissue in a controlled artificial medium.

✓ Plant tissue culture is used for:
◆ Rapid multiplication.
◆ Disease-free plants.
◆ Uniform planting material.
◆ Propagation of valuable crops.

✓ Advantage → many plants can be produced from a small amount of tissue.

title: ✓ 1.6 HEALTH & WELL-BEING
notes:
✓ Biotechnology produces important medical products.

◆ Insulin → treatment of diabetes.
◆ Growth hormone → treatment of some growth disorders.
◆ Tissue plasminogen activator → treatment of some heart attacks.
✓ Recombinant DNA technology → production of useful therapeutic proteins.

title: ✓ 1.6.1 ANTIBIOTICS
notes:
✓ Antibiotics → substances produced by microorganisms that inhibit or kill bacteria.

◆ Penicillium → penicillin.
◆ Streptomyces → streptomycin.
◆ Actinomycetes → important antibiotic producers.

◆ Bacteriostatic → stops bacterial growth.
◆ Bactericidal → kills bacteria.

✓ Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming.

title: ✓ 1.6.2 VACCINE PRODUCTION
notes:
✓ Biotechnology and microbial culture are used to produce vaccines and toxoids.

✓ Examples of organisms used in vaccine production include:
◆ Bordetella pertussis.
◆ Salmonella typhi.
◆ Vibrio cholerae.
◆ Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
◆ Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
◆ Clostridium tetani.

✓ Vaccines stimulate immunity against specific diseases.

title: ✓ 1.6.3 BIOSENSORS
notes:
✓ Biosensor → device combining a biological component with a detector to produce a measurable signal.

✓ Applications →
◆ Glucose measurement.
◆ Pollution monitoring.
◆ Food-quality testing.
◆ Detection of pathogens, toxins and DNA.

✓ Biological reaction → detectable signal.

title: ✓ 1.6.4 FORENSIC BIOLOGY
notes:
✓ Forensic biology → application of biological knowledge to crime investigation and identification.

✓ DNA → identification and comparison of biological samples.
✓ Blood, saliva and hair → biological evidence.
✓ DNA profiling → helps identify or exclude individuals.
✓ DNA analysis → also used in paternity testing.

title: ✓ 1.6.5 BIOMINING
notes:
✓ Biomining → use of microorganisms to help extract metals from ores.

✓ Biohydrometallurgy → microbial extraction of metals.

✓ Thiobacillus ferrooxidans → helps oxidize sulfide minerals and release metals.

✓ Applications → recovery of copper, iron, gold and other metals, especially from low-grade ores.

title: ✓ 1.6.6 ENVIRONMENTAL BIOTECHNOLOGY
notes:
✓ Environmental biotechnology uses organisms to manage waste and reduce pollution.

✓ Major applications:
◆ Composting.
◆ Wastewater treatment.
◆ Bioremediation.
◆ Biofuel production.
◆ Biogas production.

✓ Goal → reduce pollution and recover useful resources.

title: ✓ 1.6.7 COMPOSTING
notes:
✓ Composting → aerobic microbial decomposition of organic waste into stable, humus-like material.

✓ Bacteria + fungi → decompose organic matter.
✓ Requires oxygen.
✓ Produces compost that improves soil quality.

✓ Organic waste + microorganisms + O₂ → compost + CO₂ + H₂O.

title: ✓ 1.6.8 WASTEWATER TREATMENT
notes:
✓ BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) → amount of oxygen required by microorganisms to decompose organic matter in water.

1 Primary → physical removal + sedimentation.
2 Secondary → microorganisms decompose organic matter and reduce BOD.
3 Disinfection → treated water may be disinfected before release.

✓ Trickling filter → microbial biofilm treats wastewater.

✓ Activated sludge → aerated microbial treatment.

✓ Aim → remove pollutants and harmful microorganisms.

title: ✓ 1.6.9 BIOREMEDIATION
notes:
✓ Bioremediation → use of organisms to remove, degrade or detoxify environmental pollutants.

✓ Biodegradation → microorganisms break pollutants into simpler substances.

✓ Biotransformation → biological modification of pollutant structure.

✓ Microorganisms can also alter toxic heavy metals.

✓ Bioremediation = biological pollution control.

title: ✓ 1.6.10 BIOFUELS
notes:
✓ Biofuel → fuel produced from biological materials.

✓ Ethanol → commonly produced by microbial fermentation.

✓ Agricultural residues → can provide raw materials for biofuel production.

✓ Cellulose/hemicellulose → can be converted into fermentable sugars.

✓ Biofuels reduce dependence on fossil fuels and make use of biological waste.

title: ✓ 1.6.11 BIOGAS
notes:
✓ Biogas → gas produced by anaerobic microbial decomposition of organic matter.

✓ Main gas → methane (CH₄).
✓ Other major gas → CO₂.
✓ Methanogens → microorganisms that produce methane.

✓ Uses → cooking • heating • lighting.

✓ Anaerobic digestion → organic waste → organic acids → acetate → methane.

title: ✓ 1.7 APPLICATIONS IN INDUSTRY
notes:
✓ Industrial biotechnology uses microorganisms and their products to manufacture useful materials.

✓ Major applications:
◆ Enzyme production.
◆ Biological washing powders.
◆ Food processing.
◆ Fermentation industries.

✓ Microbial fermentation provides an efficient way to produce valuable biological products.

title: ✓ 1.7.1 INDUSTRIAL ENZYMES
notes:
◆ Proteases → remove protein stains; food and leather industries.

◆ Lipases → break down fats; detergents and food industries.

◆ Pectinases → clarify fruit juices.

◆ Amylases → break starch into sugars.

✓ Extracellular enzymes → released outside cells.

✓ Intracellular enzymes → remain inside cells and must be extracted.

title: ✓ 1.7.2 BIOLOGICAL WASHING POWDERS
notes:
✓ Biological detergents contain enzymes that break down stains.

◆ Proteases → proteins → smaller soluble products.

◆ Lipases → fats → smaller soluble products.

✓ Enzymes improve cleaning, often allowing effective washing at lower temperatures.

title: ✓ 1.8 APPLICATIONS IN AGRICULTURE
notes:
✓ Biotechnology improves agricultural productivity and pest control.

✓ Major applications → biopesticides • Ti plasmid • insect-resistant crops • pest-resistant crops • transgenic plants/animals • herbicide resistance • cloning.

title: ✓ 1.8.1 BIOPESTICIDES
notes:
✓ Biopesticides → biological organisms or their products used to control pests.

◆ Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) → produces toxins harmful to certain insect larvae.
◆ Beauveria bassiana → insect-pathogenic fungus.
◆ Metarhizium anisopliae → controls certain insects.
◆ Bacillus popilliae → biological control of some beetles.

✓ Advantage → can reduce dependence on chemical pesticides.

title: ✓ 1.8.2 Ti PLASMID AS A VECTOR
notes:
✓ Agrobacterium tumefaciens contains a Ti plasmid that can transfer genes into plant cells.

✓ Basic steps:
1 Insert desired gene into Ti plasmid.
2 Introduce plasmid into plant cells.
3 Select transformed cells.
4 Regenerate complete plants.

✓ Ti plasmid → important vector for plant genetic engineering.

title: ✓ 1.8.3 INSECT & PEST-RESISTANT CROPS
notes:
✓ Genetic engineering can give crops resistance to specific pests.

✓ Bt crops → contain genes from Bacillus thuringiensis.

◆ Examples → Bt maize, Bt cotton.

✓ Benefits → reduced insect damage + potentially higher yield + reduced insecticide use.

✓ Concerns → pest resistance, effects on non-target organisms and gene transfer.

title: ✓ 1.8.4 HERBICIDE-RESISTANT CROPS
notes:
✓ Herbicide-resistant crops are genetically modified to tolerate a particular herbicide.

✓ Herbicide → chemical used to control weeds.

✓ Resistant crop → survives herbicide application while susceptible weeds die.

✓ Benefit → easier and more efficient weed control.

title: ✓ 1.8.5 TRANSGENIC ANIMALS
notes:
✓ Transgenic animals → animals containing an introduced gene.

✓ Applications:
◆ Production of useful proteins.
◆ Improved livestock traits.
◆ Medical research.
◆ Study of genes and diseases.

✓ Examples → sheep • goats • chickens • mice.

title: ✓ 1.8.6 TRANSGENIC PLANTS
notes:
✓ Transgenic plants → plants containing introduced genetic material.

✓ Possible traits:
◆ Pest resistance.
◆ Disease resistance.
◆ Herbicide resistance.
◆ Drought tolerance.
◆ Improved nutrition.
◆ Pharmaceutical production.

title: ✓ 1.8.7 CLONING
notes:
✓ Cloning → production of genetically identical copies of genes, cells or organisms.

✓ Clone → genetically identical copy.

✓ Gene cloning → produces copies of a gene.

✓ Reproductive cloning → produces a genetically similar organism.

✓ Key idea → cloning creates genetically identical biological copies.

title: ✓ 1.8.8 ANIMAL CLONING
notes:
✓ Somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT):
1 Remove nucleus from an egg cell.
2 Insert nucleus from a donor body cell.
3 Activate the egg to begin division.
4 Develop embryo.
5 Implant embryo into a surrogate mother.
6 Offspring is genetically identical to the nuclear donor.

✓ Dolly the sheep → famous example of cloning from an adult somatic cell.

title: ✓ 1.9 BIOLOGICAL WARFARE
notes:
✓ Biological warfare → deliberate use of biological agents or toxins to harm humans, animals or plants.

✓ Agents may include bacteria, viruses, fungi or biological toxins.

✓ Effects → disease, disability, death or environmental damage.

✓ Biological warfare raises serious ethical, environmental and security concerns.

title: ✓ UNIT 1 QUICK REVISION
notes:
✓ Conservation → protection and wise use of natural resources.

✓ Food security → sufficient, safe and nutritious food for all.

✓ Sustainable development → economic + social + environmental balance.

✓ Biotechnology → useful application of living organisms/biological processes.

✓ Genetic engineering → deliberate modification/transfer of DNA.

✓ Transgene → transferred gene.

✓ Fermentation → microbial conversion of substrates into useful products.

✓ Antibiotics → substances that inhibit/kill bacteria.

✓ Biosensor → biological component + detector.

✓ Biomining → microbial metal extraction.

✓ Bioremediation → biological removal/degradation of pollutants.

✓ Biofuel → fuel from biological materials.

✓ Biogas → mainly methane from anaerobic digestion.

✓ Tissue culture → controlled growth of cells/tissues.

✓ Biopesticide → biological pest control.

✓ Ti plasmid → plant gene-transfer vector.

✓ Bt crop → insect-resistant genetically modified crop.

✓ Clone → genetically identical copy.
